chapter: Swing, singers, Ed Fox and recordings
title: A congenial big band: the Wet and the Dry
summary: No fights; drinkers vs. pot smokers.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yeah, family-type thing. It was a surprisingly congenial band to be as large as it was, 16 pieces, you know, 16 men. No arguments, fights, nothing, the whole time I was with the band.
Any cliques?
No, except for what we called the Wet and the Dry.
Those who drank and those who didn't?
Yeah.
What was the larger group?
Hey, you know it was about half and half.
Really?
Uh-huh.
Was there much pot smoking?
That was the Dry half.
Oh, okay, now I get you. I thought you meant non-drinkers.
No.
I think maybe Chuck mentioned that division to me one time.
Yeah. Even with that division, we all got along fine.
The Wet and the Dry.
I used to get -- well, you know, I never did go for pot, but I used to like to get what we'd call a contact high.
Yeah. Well, that's still pretty much the way things are. Hasn't changed too much.
Yeah, same thing. Nothing changes.
Yeah.
As far as musicians is concerned.
Right, right. The social behavior, as we would say, of musicians is pretty much the same.
